title_original: Open Call – 4th edition of the Ronan Guillou Grant
excerpt_original: For its fourth edition, the Ronan Guillou Grant is launching a call for proposals for a creative grant open to professional photographers from Europe […] Cet article Open Call – 4th edition of the Ronan Guillou Grant est apparu en premier sur The Eye of Photography Magazine .

blocks.text: For its fourth edition, the Ronan Guillou Grant is launching a call for proposals for a creative grant open to professional photographers from Europe and the southern shores of the Mediterranean.

The Ronan Guillou Grant, created by the non-profit organisation Eyes Wide Open (a label of The Eyes), explores the relationship between human and the sea, with the aim of restoring a shared sense of purpose to our cultures and examining the key challenges facing the sea today.

The project must examine the challenges facing our future in relation to the marine world and/or present a progressive, committed or activist vision capable of contributing to collective awareness. In particular, it may address issues relating to ecology, human activities, the transmission of knowledge and the concept of heritage, economic and geopolitical challenges, or the relationships between the Occitan region and other areas of the Mediterranean basin.

The photographer awarded the grant will receive €4,000 (comprising €3,000 in remuneration and €1,000 expenses) to carry out their project, which may take place over a period of five months, including two months on location. An exhibition is planned for September 2027 at the Musée de l’Étang de Thau in Bouzigues, as part of the 2nd edition of the FLOW Biennial (18 September – 31 October 2027).
The 4th edition of the Ronan Guillou Fellowship is supported by Sète Agglopôle Méditerranée, M28-Terres de culture, the Musée de l’Étang de Thau, Hahnemühle and the Tomoé laboratory.

Call for applications: October 1st to November 15th 2026 (6.00 pm) Jury: late November 2026 Announcement of the winner: during December (the winner will be notified in advance) Residency in Sète: between February and June 2027 (2 months on site) Exhibition: September 2027 at the Musée de l’Étang de Thau as part of the FLOW Biennial
